Synopsis:
Serves as the front desk for the House of Grief. Encourages the player to partake of their services in exchange for a fee. Secretly a Sharran agent seeking to lure in the unwitting.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_HouseOfGrief_OM_Shadowheart_COM.json: Attendant serving as the front desk for the House of Grief. Recognises Shadowheart and urges her to enter the room beyond and submit to the Mapping of the heart, and beyond it, her return to the Sharran grotto.
- LOW_HouseOfGrief_GriefAttendant.json: Mirie is the polite receptionist at the House of Grief, seating visitors and initiating its rituals—most notably the "Mapping of the Heart" and the Unburdening—while urging patrons to pay for relief from sorrow, anger, and troubling memories. Her lines repeatedly press that the player "needs" help and claim she senses inner turmoil, which is part sales pitch and part practiced sympathy to coax customers into the room. Off‑screen the House of Grief functions as a hospice‑style front; Mirie is secretly a Sharran agent using this role to identify and lure unwitting people for Shar’s purposes. She also keeps tabs on recent local events and can flatter or invoke the player’s deeds (e.g., a victory over Viconia) to build trust and prompt a booking.
- LOW_HouseOfGrief_OM_Shadowheart_AOM_OOM.json: Serves as the front desk for the House of Grief. Will reject any attempts to book an appointment unless Shadowheart is there.
- LOW_HouseOfGrief_ConfusedMerchant.json: A confused merchant still lingers by the House of Grief after his unburdening (he came for grief counseling, only to have his memories stolen). Players can learn he is missing memories as a clue towards the House of Grief's true purpose.
- LOW_HouseOfGrief_GriefGuard_000.json: Afara is the House of Grief’s outwardly warm usher — she greets and guides visitors in a serene, comforting tone while actually acting as a sentry who watches and assesses those who enter. The single-node lines can play as a generic, calming welcome or as a more personal, groveling recognition that implies prior acquaintance (one-time peer now subordinated). Off-screen, the House is an institution people enter expecting consolation, and companions—especially anyone alerted by Shadowheart’s book about a nearby Shar temple and a “shadow curse”—may therefore react with unease or suspicion despite Afara’s pleasant words. Because this is a one-line node, her greeting both masks scrutiny and establishes whether she recognizes or places importance on the visitor.

Mirie is the polite receptionist at the House of Grief, seating visitors and initiating its rituals—most notably the "Mapping of the Heart" and the Unburdening—while urging patrons to pay for relief from sorrow, anger, and troubling memories. Her lines repeatedly press that the player "needs" help and claim she senses inner turmoil, which is part sales pitch and part practiced sympathy to coax customers into the room. Off‑screen the House of Grief functions as a hospice‑style front; Mirie is secretly a Sharran agent using this role to identify and lure unwitting people for Shar’s purposes. She also keeps tabs on recent local events and can flatter or invoke the player’s deeds (e.g., a victory over Viconia) to build trust and prompt a booking.
Serves as the front desk for the House of Grief. Will reject any attempts to book an appointment unless Shadowheart is there.

A confused merchant still lingers by the House of Grief after his unburdening (he came for grief counseling, only to have his memories stolen). Players can learn he is missing memories as a clue towards the House of Grief's true purpose.

Afara is the House of Grief’s outwardly warm usher — she greets and guides visitors in a serene, comforting tone while actually acting as a sentry who watches and assesses those who enter. The single-node lines can play as a generic, calming welcome or as a more personal, groveling recognition that implies prior acquaintance (one-time peer now subordinated). context: Mirie is the polite receptionist who runs the front desk at the House of Grief, seating visitors and pushing its rituals—the Mapping of the Heart and the Unburdening—while insisting the player “needs” relief and urging them to book and pay. She flatters or invokes recent deeds (for example praising a victory over Viconia) and claims to sense inner turmoil as part sales pitch and part practiced sympathy to coax patrons into the room. Off‑screen, the House functions as a hospice‑style front and rumors (and a lingering confused merchant) imply the Unburdening can cost memories rather than simply soothe them. Unknown to most visitors, Mirie is secretly an agent of Shar, using her role to identify and lure unwitting people toward the Sharran grotto; in some variants she will even insist Shadowheart be present for certain appointments.
